contributions.head: ea2b6fa4d6479813c36ca0c0396c8d06437fb486
contributions.title: Pay the two-target CRT stencil producer and join its repair mask
contributions.claim_excerpt:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds `research/crt-two-target-stencil/`: a paid producer for two ordered disjoint CRT guard windows, consuming seven protected unary geometry words. Its actual stencil feeds the unchanged dense scanner, and that mask feeds the retained reverse-key repair. This answers PR4644 open question 1: the previous joined producer covered one target, although the scanner and record repair already accepted externally supplied multi-target data.

For every admitted `G>=1, H>=2G, K>=G+4, J1>=J0+K, Y>=J1+K`, the written proof derives the exact stencil, union-of-failures hole mask, cleanup and producer invoice:

```
46H+20K+38Y-24G-J0+12J1+12B+438 <= 70L+438,  L=2H+Y+B.
```

The producer/scanner uses 21 fixed tape roles and at most `8ML+15M+83L+456` read/write/unit-move actions, `M=2^L`. The caller erases its owned stencil for another `5L+7` actions. Both source functions must omit both active target bits. Borrowed geometry remains unchanged; private words, scanner counter, consumed mask and repair scratch are erased and heads returned.

This is a local interface/cost proof with finite implementation evidence. Existing reverse algebra and repair tariff remain cited; the opaque-record repair model, host key arithmetic and finite-control transitions do not become a unified binary invoice. Caller descriptor construction/transport, variable target count, last-K boundaries and complete supplier admission remain open. No new κ or selected-frontier change; conditional κ=.00302015 remains selected.

contributions.head: 785ecde9e87bfd40bc4279e1cee2b06c988530fc
contributions.title: Screen the selected mixed-target moment with certified adaptive bounds
contributions.claim_excerpt:
The selected PR4470 raw invoice has variable target and paid moment sums, so the older fixed-target screening model cannot be carried over unchanged. This package freezes the published invoice and tests certified alternating-Taylor bounds on their signed difference. It adds a sign-only adaptive screen and a rejection-only gate that retains the original full interval calculation for accepted candidates.

Seven fixtures agree with two other exponential enclosures, including the unchanged upstream arithmetic engine. In 252 fresh-process measurements, the rejection-only gate saves a median paired 32–35% on the two rejecting fixtures and costs about 11% more on the accepting fixture. These are three fixed test rates, not a candidate population or a complete replay speedup. The first roughly 10 seconds overlapped with a verification run; the timing file and README disclose this and uncontrolled host contention.
